**ClickHouse** is an open-source [column-oriented DBMS](/wiki/Column-oriented_DBMS "Column-oriented DBMS") (columnar database management system) for [online analytical processing](/wiki/Online_analytical_processing "Online analytical processing") (OLAP) that allows users to generate analytical reports using structured query language ([SQL](/wiki/SQL "SQL")) queries in real-time. ClickHouse Inc. is headquartered in the [San Francisco Bay Area](/wiki/San_Francisco_Bay_Area "San Francisco Bay Area") with the subsidiary, ClickHouse B.V., based in [Amsterdam](/wiki/Amsterdam "Amsterdam"), [Netherlands](/wiki/Netherlands "Netherlands").

title: ClickHouse
text:
**ClickHouse** is an open-source [column-oriented DBMS](/wiki/Column-oriented_DBMS "Column-oriented DBMS") (columnar database management system) for [online analytical processing](/wiki/Online_analytical_processing "Online analytical processing") (OLAP) that allows users to generate analytical reports using structured query language ([SQL](/wiki/SQL "SQL")) queries in real-time. ClickHouse Inc. is headquartered in the [San Francisco Bay Area](/wiki/San_Francisco_Bay_Area "San Francisco Bay Area") with the subsidiary, ClickHouse B.V., based in [Amsterdam](/wiki/Amsterdam "Amsterdam"), [Netherlands](/wiki/Netherlands "Netherlands").

ClickHouse, Inc. was incorporated in San Francisco, California, in September 2021 to commercialize the open-source ClickHouse database. The company was initially funded with US$50 million from [Index Ventures](/wiki/Index_Ventures "Index Ventures") and [Benchmark Capital](/wiki/Benchmark_Capital "Benchmark Capital"), with participation from Yandex N.V. and others.[[2]](#cite_note-2) On 28 October 2021, the company announced a US$250 million Series B funding round at a valuation of US$2 billion, led by [Coatue Management](/wiki/Coatue_Management "Coatue Management"), [Altimeter Capital](/wiki/Altimeter_Capital "Altimeter Capital"), and others.[[3]](#cite_note-3)

title: ClickHouse
text:
ClickHouse, Inc. was incorporated in San Francisco, California, in September 2021 to commercialize the open-source ClickHouse database. The company was initially funded with US$50 million from [Index Ventures](/wiki/Index_Ventures "Index Ventures") and [Benchmark Capital](/wiki/Benchmark_Capital "Benchmark Capital"), with participation from Yandex N.V. and others.[[2]](#cite_note-2) On 28 October 2021, the company announced a US$250 million Series B funding round at a valuation of US$2 billion, led by [Coatue Management](/wiki/Coatue_Management "Coatue Management"), [Altimeter Capital](/wiki/Altimeter_Capital "Altimeter Capital"), and others.[[3]](#cite_note-3)

In May 2025, ClickHouse raised US$350 million in a [Series C](/wiki/Series_C "Series C") funding round led by [Khosla Ventures](/wiki/Khosla_Ventures "Khosla Ventures"), with participation from BOND, IVP, Battery Ventures, Bessemer Venture Partners, and existing investors including [Index Ventures](/wiki/Index_Ventures "Index Ventures"), [Lightspeed Venture Partners](/wiki/Lightspeed_Venture_Partners "Lightspeed Venture Partners"), GIC, [Benchmark Capital](/wiki/Benchmark_Capital "Benchmark Capital"), [Coatue Management](/wiki/Coatue_Management "Coatue Management"), [FirstMark Capital](/wiki/FirstMark_Capital "FirstMark Capital"), and [Nebius Group](/wiki/Nebius_Group "Nebius Group"). The round valued the company at approximately US$6.35 billion and brought total funding to more than US$650 million.[[4]](#cite_note-4)

title: ClickHouse
text:
## History

ClickHouse’s technology was first developed at [Yandex](/wiki/Yandex "Yandex"), Russia's largest technology company.[[5]](#cite_note-5) In 2009, Alexey Milovidov and developers started an experimental project to check the hypothesis if it was viable to generate analytical reports in real-time from non-[aggregated data](/wiki/Aggregate_data "Aggregate data") that is also constantly added in real-time. The developers spent 3 years to prove this hypothesis, and in 2012 ClickHouse launched in production for the first time to power [Yandex.Metrica](/wiki/Yandex.Metrica "Yandex.Metrica").[*[citation needed](/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*]

Since ClickHouse became available as open source in 2016, its popularity has grown, as evidenced through adoption by industry-leading companies like [Uber](/wiki/Uber "Uber"), [Comcast](/wiki/Comcast "Comcast"), [eBay](/wiki/EBay "EBay"), and [Cisco](/wiki/Cisco "Cisco").[[6]](#cite_note-6) ClickHouse was also implemented at [CERN's](/wiki/CERN "CERN") [LHCb experiment](/wiki/LHCb_experiment "LHCb experiment") to store and process [metadata](/wiki/Metadata "Metadata") on 10 billion events with over 1000 attributes per event.[*[citation needed](/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*]

title: ClickHouse
text:
### Acquisitions

ClickHouse, Inc. has made the following acquisitions:

- **Arctype** — October 2022. Arctype's SQL client was integrated into ClickHouse Cloud to provide a web-based interface that formed the basis for the Cloud Console.[[7]](#cite_note-7)
- **chDB** — March 2024. chDB is an in-process OLAP SQL engine that embeds the ClickHouse engine as a [library](/wiki/Software_library "Software library"), allowing analytical queries to run inside a host application rather than against a separate server.[[8]](#cite_note-8)
- **PeerDB** — July 2024. PeerDB provides change data capture (CDC) technology that enables replication from [PostgreSQL](/wiki/PostgreSQL "PostgreSQL") into ClickHouse, expanding real-time analytics capabilities. ClickHouse, Inc. offers a hosted version of PeerDB through ClickPipes, a managed ingestion service for ClickHouse Cloud that supports seamless integration with Postgres sources.[[9]](#cite_note-9)
- **HyperDX** — March 2025. HyperDX is an open-source observability platform built on ClickHouse, providing a user interface and observability tooling that were integrated into ClickHouse's observability stack. HyperDX now serves as the primary UI for ClickStack, an open-source observability stack based on ClickHouse.[[10]](#cite_note-10)
- **LibreChat** — November 2025. LibreChat is an open-source platform that provides a unified chat interface for interacting with large language models. It became part of ClickHouse's open-source "Agentic Data Stack".[[11]](#cite_note-11)
- **Langfuse** — January 2026. Langfuse is an open-source platform for large language model observability, evaluation, and prompt management. The acquisition was announced alongside a US$400 million Series D funding round.[[12]](#cite_note-12)[[13]](#cite_note-13)
